text:
How Cardiff are changing Swansea derby narrative
- Published
It can be difficult to change the narrative in sport. Take Cardiff City and their rivalry with Swansea City.
For years, a certain idea had taken hold, that the Swans - their players, staff, the club as a whole - had a better understanding of what the south Wales derby meant, and that innate grasp of its significance had given them the upper hand.
Results have supported the theory. Since a nine-year period at the start of this century where there were no derbies, Swansea have won 11 out of 21 and become the first team in the fixture's century-long history to do the double – that is, to win both league meetings in one season – before repeating the feat the following campaign.
Once a pattern is set in motion, it can take some stopping but, by winning their past two home derbies, Cardiff felt the tide might have been turning.
Granted, the most recent of those triumphs still ended with their relegation to League One two seasons ago, but there was at least a feeling that the hoodoo had been lifted.
Nearly two years have passed since the last south Wales derby. In that time, Cardiff have made an instant return to the Championship under head coach Brian Barry-Murphy, who has introduced a refreshingly bold and attacking style of play, built around a core of young local players.
They are still behind their neighbours, though.
Cardiff travel to Swansea on Sunday 17th in the table, nine places and nine points adrift of their opponents.
The Bluebirds have caught the eye with their performances this season but, for all their ambition and stylish dominance of possession, the defensive risks that come attached mean that they are still searching for a first away win of the campaign.
You have to go back nine derbies for the last time Cardiff won in Swansea, and a decade further back again for the last time they triumphed there with fans present.
What an opportunity this weekend's reunion presents, then, to shift another narrative.
"You have to accept it's a different game," says Barry-Murphy, preparing for his first south Wales derby.
"It's not a normal game, and I think if you try to make out as if it's just another game, you're preparing for something that's not going to happen.
"This is a totally different fixture for our players because the atmosphere is going to be totally different.
"We have to show that we have the characteristics and personality to perform the way we want to perform in that heat of battle and show who we want to be as a team.
"We're a very aggressive team and have a lot of daring players who play on the front foot. Our intention on Sunday, despite whatever the opposition do, is to show that version of ourselves."
Rivals flip the script with managerial upheaval
There will be a marked difference between this freewheeling Cardiff side and the previous, cagier iterations to make the short trip down the M4 to face Swansea, who have built their identity around a progressive football philosophy over the past 20 years.
If that represents a hint of convergence between the two rivals on the pitch, then one area where the clubs have certainly flipped the script is managerial upheaval.
For more than a decade, this fixture had symbolised the dysfunctional running of Cardiff; between 2011 and 2023, none of their managers had lasted long enough to oversee two derbies in one season.
Erol Bulut bucked that trend, only to get sacked less than a month after he was sent off during a 1-1 draw at the Swansea.com Stadium.
Now, Cardiff finally have the stability they have craved – and it is Swansea who have to contend with changes in the dugout.
The Swans are looking for a third permanent head coach since the Bluebirds appointed Barry-Murphy in the summer of 2025.
It is a far cry from the situation four years ago.
After the third of four successive wins over Cardiff, Swansea's head coach at the time, Russell Martin, said their greater stability was one of the reasons for their success against rivals who had a different man at the helm for each of those four defeats.
Former captain Ashley Williams is in charge of the Swans temporarily - assisted by fellow club greats Joe Allen, Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary - while they look for a full-time successor to Vitor Matos.
Given the abrupt nature of Matos' departure and the ongoing search for his replacement, could this be a good time to face Swansea?
"Maybe, maybe not," says Cardiff vice-captain Rubin Colwill, who is almost certain to wear the armband on Sunday.
"I think the focus for us is us. We've worked really hard, we're really nailed on in what we're doing, and I think that's the most important thing, regardless of any situation that they're experiencing at the moment."
Colwill embodies Cardiff's new ethos: the creative heartbeat of the team and a young, maturing Welsh talent flourishing with the greater responsibility he has been given by Barry-Murphy.
Growing up as a Bluebirds fan in Neath, closer to Swansea than the Welsh capital, the 24-year-old also has a strong sense of what this rivalry means on both sides of the divide.
Colwill featured from the bench in Cardiff's thumping 3-0 win when the teams last met in January 2025, while he was an unused substitute when his side won in Swansea five years ago.
He has yet to start a south Wales derby but, as a leader of this new-look Cardiff, Colwill is bound to put that right on Sunday.
"We're all really comfortable with this style of play," he says.
"It's just fine-tuning that last little bit and we'll turn those dominant performances into big victories. Hopefully that will start on Sunday."
digest_he: עבור שנים רבות, סוונסי סיטי שלטה בדרבי של דרום ויילס והחזיקה ביתרון פסיכולוגי ומקצועי על פני היריבה המושבעת קרדיף סיטי. התוצאות לאורך השנים תמכו במגמה זו, כאשר סוונסי רשמה ניצחונות רבים יותר ואף השלימה פעמיים רצופות ניצחונות כפולים בשורות הליגה. עם זאת, התקופה הגיע לנקודת מפנה כאשר קרדיף ניצחה בשני משחקי הבית האחרונים בין הקבוצות, וכעת היא מגיעה למפגש בהדרכת המאמן בריאן בארי-מרפי, שהטמיע סגנון משחק התקפי ושאיפתני המבוסס על שחקנים צעירים ומקומיים.  הקבוצה מדורגת כיום במקום ה-17 בטבלה, תשע נקודות מאחורי סוונסי, והיא עדיין מחפשת אחר ניצחון החוץ הראשון שלה העונה בשל הסיכונים ההגנתיים הנלווים לסגנונה ההתקפי. מנגד, סוונסי חווה תקופה של חוסר יציבות ניהולית ומחפשת מאמן קבוע שלישי מאז הקיץ, כאשר שחקן העבר אשלי וויליאמס משמש כמאמן זמני. קשר קרדיף, רובין קולוויל, מדגיש כי קבוצתו ממוקדת בעצמה ומוכנה להציג את האופי והזהות ההתקפית שלה על כר הדשא במטרה להפוך את הקערה על פיה.
